naive.title: Gate the clock with a phase flop on the ordinary clock tree
naive.text: Half rate means an ICG (clock gate) at the root that passes every other edge, enabled by a phase flop that toggles. Clock-tree synthesis balanced that phase flop with the 93,415 sinks sinks below the gate, so it launched at 1,110.8 ps while the ICG pin it feeds sees its clock at about 153.3 ps: one path, phase flop to ICG enable, failed by −474.7 ps. Every other path class had at least +96.0 ps.

trick.title: HALF_PHL: put the phase flop on the gate's own clock net
trick.text: The phase flop now drives only the ICG enable, and a pre-CTS hook moves it onto the net that clocks the ICG, beside it, so launch and gate share one clock arrival. Everything else that needs the phase (the half-cycle marker, output qualifier and capture enables) reads ph_d = t XNOR t_d, rebuilt from two flops on balanced leaves; an assertion checks ph_d equals the phase on every cycle. It adds two flops and one XNOR and zero cycles.

cards.evidence: Transaction-level exact: 456 partials identical to the original element; the three negative mutants (front pair, half qualifier, phase mismatch) all fail. The element itself passes the independent numerical gate on 456 rows.
cards.price: Half rate doubles BF16 field-phase time: −7.68% AR and −6.31% MTP (upper bound). BF pairs must then be BF-dedicated, which adds 6 stages and 24 dies.

cards.title: A 128-way sibling search split into two cycles
cards.summary: With several field operations in flight, partial sums come back out of order. The root finds each partial's sibling among 128 waiting entries and adds them in the golden order. That search cannot happen in one clock, so it is split in two without changing a single pairing decision.

cards.problem: Each root holds up to 128 entries waiting partial sums. Finding the sibling of an arriving partial is a 4,096 bits/cycle compare, then a priority encode, then a buffer update, and the next arrival depends on that update. There are 128 roots such roots on a die.

naive.title: Search, encode and update in one cycle
naive.text: The native root does compare, encode and update in the same cycle. At 833 ps that is a 128-input compare, a 128-way priority encoder and a write-back in series: it does not fit, and the design model says so before any route (microarch obligation in design.json).

trick.title: Register the match vectors, forward the last update
trick.text: Stage A registers the 128-bit match and free vectors computed from a registered queue head. Stage B encodes and updates. An entry inserted or removed by B on this edge is forwarded into A's view on the same edge, so A never acts on stale state and the pairing decisions are identical to the native root. The fallback, stage C, fetches the paired entry's operands one edge after the decision from a registered hit index: safe because a slot removed in B(t) can only be rewritten by an insert decided in B(t+1).

cards.evidence: Exact against the unchanged native root on 384 roots. The two negative controls (no insert forwarding, wrong sibling) fail as required. Measured added latency: 1 cycle isolated, 2 cycles for a two-leaf root, 4 cycles for an eight-leaf root.
cards.price: Latency only: one cycle per root decision pass. Charged as an upper bound in the DS ledger (every phase exposes one eight-leaf root). Added state 49,536 bits for all roots.

steps.note: Cycle t: compare the tag against all 128 entries...
...encode the hit...
...and write the buffer, all inside one 833 ps period. It does not fit.
Cycle t: A registers which of the 128 entries match and which are free.
Cycle t+1: B encodes the hit and updates the buffer.
The entry B inserted or freed on this edge is forwarded into A on the same edge: no stale decision.
The pair goes to the adder in golden order: +1 cycle a pass (measured 1 cycle / 2 cycles / 4 cycles).
Stage C (fallback) reads the operands one edge later from a registered hit index.

naive.title: Close each loop in one cycle
naive.text: The streamer read a ROM word, compared its need against what the x-buffer had, chose the next ROM address and read again, all in one cycle. Behavioural + and <= became ripple adders.

trick.title: A reader that runs ahead, and a fully registered return
trick.text: A stream-ROM reader works one operation ahead in four stages (address, word, derived need/flags) and pushes words into a queue with 8 credits, so the streamer's advance test is a short compare on kept copies. Beat assembly reads from registered, replicated indices. The return path is region-local: register, select from a per-16-region table replica, add the address with a prefix adder, write. Row counts come from registered tags through a popcount tree.

cards.evidence: Exact on every region with released-checkpoint rows: 20,160 runs and 249,920 rows, 0 mismatches. The issue rule holds on 9,072 op pairs. New screens: SS +18.7 ps (PQ=0, R=16) with FF −0.18 ps on one pin, SS +14.0 ps (PQ=1, R=16). The redesign also found an inherited tag bug that failed 55 of 60 runs.

cards.title: How many element pairs fit in a field column
cards.element: S81 field frame (mixed BF / q slots)
cards.summary: A field column has a fixed height. BF16 pairs and FP8/FP4 q pairs need different slot heights, so the number of pairs a die holds depends on how they are packed. The legal answer turned out lower than the plan.
cards.status_basis: unified ledger gate field_phases_1792: the 1,792 geometry's field phases are unmeasured
cards.problem: The plan asked for 2,304 pairs a die with mixed slots (q slots 183.6 um, BF slots 198.72 um). The legal-fit check sums the slot heights of the tallest column against the frame: 2,887.57 um available.

naive.title: Pack the most pairs (mixed183, 2,304 pairs)
naive.text: Shorter q slots looked like they fit more pairs. The tallest column needs 2,982.96 um against 2,887.57 um: not a legal fit.

trick.title: Size the slots to what routes, then count dies
trick.text: The q slot that routes is taller (221.4 um), which caps a die at 1,792 pairs. Uniform 198.72 um slots fit 2,048 (2,808.00 um). Instead of squeezing, the design keeps the routable slot and adds dies: the 1,792 mapping needs 120 stages with BF-dedicated half-rate pairs or 98 stages with shared pairs.

cards.evidence: Legal-fit sums from the geometry model (frame 2,887.57 um): uniform198 2,808.00 um fits; mixed183 2,982.96 um and mixed221 at 2,048 pairs 2,950.56 um do not. Both 1,792 mappings pass capacity on the released checkpoint declarations.
cards.price: Extra stages add board hops: the half-dedicated mapping adds 29.5 us of AR latency in the ledger (priced, not yet composed with measured field phases).

cards.title: Crossing between clock regions without synchronising pointers
cards.summary: Regions of a ROM die share one clock frequency but not one phase. The crossing FIFO writes a slot every cycle no matter what, places its read pointer once at reset, then just counts, and guard slots stop it the moment the phase drifts too far.

cards.problem: A synchronous register between two regions would need their clock trees matched to within the hold and setup window at 833 ps across the die. They come from one reference but their phase is unknown and wanders slowly (about 192 ps central).

naive.title: A general asynchronous FIFO
naive.text: Gray-coded pointers synchronised every cycle cost several cycles each way, and the pointer compare sits on the data path. Same-frequency regions do not need any of that.

trick.title: Always write, place once, guard the window
trick.text: The writer's counter never stops: it writes slot wc every cycle, valid or not. At alignment the reader samples the writer's Gray count on both its rising and falling edge, learns which half-period the phase sits in, and sets its pointer so every slot is read OFFSET periods after it was written. From then on the pointer only increments. Each cycle it samples the lap bit of two guard slots on the opposite edge; if the lag drifts out of the window, a sticky fault stops delivery and credit (fail closed).

cards.evidence: Closed: SS 29.6 / FF 27.4 ps, DRC 0 (results/closure_loop/s81-meso-d8g1-c20d75e28/verdict.json). Bench: depth-4 positive 52/52 runs clean; an offset mutant faults as it must.
cards.price: Two cycles a crossing (d8g1: depth 8, offset 4, guard 1); a field round trip crosses twice (+4 in the DS ledger).

steps.note: Every pointer update crosses through synchronisers...
...and the compare sits in front of every read: cycles each way.

trick.note: Writer fills one slot every cycle; the reader consumes the slot written OFFSET periods ago; the guard slot is sampled on the opposite edge.

trick.title: A combinational step that is exactly IEEE
trick.text: All operands are non-negative, so the adders drop the cancellation path. Division is a multiply by a table-seeded reciprocal checked by two exact remainder signs, which picks the correctly rounded quotient. cards.summary: On a GPU, a matrix unit's results go to memory and the next kernel reads them back. Here the matrix units (SMs) send result rows straight into the vector unit's ingress FIFOs through relay stations, so the round trip through memory disappears.

cards.problem: The ROM macro's clk->q is 739 ps to 834 ps at SS, and the tile reads a bank every cycle, so the output cannot be held for two cycles. The tile routed at SS −787.7 ps.

naive.title: Capture the macro output in the same cycle

trick.title: ROM_PIPE: relay the request, capture at the pins, clock the macro early
trick.text: The request (bank enable and address) goes through relay stages, one kept copy per bank group, so it arrives from beside the macros. The macro clock is landed early by CTS (a CTS-only 250 ps insertion view), giving the read useful skew; the request path pays the same skew, which the relays absorb. The capture register sits at the macro pins with no enable, then one stage does the INT8-to-BF16 expansion and the group OR, then a relay into the engine. The other variant uses half-depth banks (clk->q 604 ps) so a balanced clock closes the single-cycle capture.

cards.evidence: Exactness benches pass with the ROM_MUT negative control failing (capture bank select one edge early). The routes are queued; the card switches to closed when a verdict lands.

cards.title: Link credits sized to the round trip
cards.summary: A credit link can only keep as many words in flight as it has credits. Across the forwarded path a credit takes 117 cycles to come back, so 8 credits sustain 0.068 words a cycle of the link; 128 credits keep it at full rate.
cards.status_basis: exact gate passes on two simulators; the hub and receive-buffer routes are queued

trick.title: Credits >= round trip (Little's law)
trick.text: Give the receiver a 128-word buffer at each strip end and the sender 128 credits: more than the 117 cycles round trip, so a credit is always back before it is needed.

cards.title: An all-reduce split by an 8-bit counter
cards.summary: Every Qwen layer runs two all-reduces of 256 words across four dies. Each one ran as two serial halves, paying the link fill and drain twice. The cause was not bandwidth or credits: the descriptor's 8-bit count could not say 256.
cards.status_basis: measured bit-exact on the TP4 runtime; no new hardware
cards.problem: Each all-reduce took 987 cycles. Each half paid the link latency (339 cycles one way) and the fold before the sequencer moved on.

naive.text: The program generator split every 256-word all-reduce into two descriptors because the count field is 8 bits, and the sequencer runs one descriptor at a time.

trick.title: Count 0 means 256
trick.text: The default-off ENABLE_AR256 path decodes a count of 0 as 256, so the whole vector goes as one stream. The collective FIFO depth follows Little's law: a 256-word vector never has more than 256 outstanding, so depth 256 streams at link rate.

cards.evidence: Bit-exact against the retained terminal: layer 4,668 cycles → 3,930 cycles. Per all-reduce 987 cycles → 624 cycles. Depth 128 measured 1,176 cycles (credit stalls); 256 and above stream without stalls.
cards.price: None: no RTL change, only the program and a FIFO depth. Projected gain 18.4% per user.

trick.title: Oldest-first shift queue, registered eligibility
trick.text: Writes sit in a 4-deep one-hot queue ordered by age; a pop shifts the queue (only on a consumed write), so "oldest" is always position 0. Bank eligibility is computed and registered a cycle earlier. Inputs and outputs are captured in flops.

cards.evidence: Exact on all 32 PCs (model before RTL; qualification record). The first SHIFT route is at SS −88.9 ps, still short of +15.
cards.price: 3 edges added from request to PHY: 144 cycles/token worst case, 0.066% of the token.

cards.title: Why the weights are ROM: the Taalas HC1 anchor
cards.summary: The ROM designs follow the only shipping evidence for a chip with all weights on die: Taalas HC1. A via-programmed ROM cell is a fraction of an SRAM cell, so a whole model fits beside the multipliers and no weight is ever fetched.
cards.status_basis: published anchor plus a measured bitcell

facts.label: ROM / 6T SRAM cell area, ASAP7
facts.src: configs/hardware/technology.json rom note: measured ratio at ASAP7 (results/asap7_physical/bitcell_density/bitcell_density.json)

facts.label: ROM / 6T SRAM cell area, 130 nm
facts.src: configs/hardware/technology.json rom note: measured ratio at 130 nm (results/spice/ihp_sg13g2_bitcell/bitcell.json)

cards.problem: Decode at batch 1 reads every weight once per token. From HBM that is a bandwidth wall; from on-die SRAM the model does not fit.

naive.title: Weights in SRAM or streamed from HBM
naive.text: SRAM is too big per bit to hold an 8B model on a reticle; HBM makes every token wait on DRAM bandwidth.

trick.title: Hard-wire the weights in ROM beside the multipliers
trick.text: A via-programmed NOR ROM cell measured 0.25 x SRAM the area of a 6T SRAM cell at ASAP7 (0.1298 x SRAM at 130 nm). HC1 shows the result at product scale: 815 mm2 die, all Llama 3.1 8B weights on die, 16,960 tok/s per user at batch 1.

cards.evidence: HC1 figures are published or reported (sources in the expander); the bitcell ratios are this repository's layout measurements.
cards.price: The model is fixed at manufacture; KV still lives in HBM beside the dies.

steps.note: One SRAM cell per bit.

cards.title: A wire reaches about half a millimetre per clock
cards.summary: At 1.2 GHz on the slow corner, a routed signal travels only about half a millimetre per clock. Every die-level path is therefore a chain of registered stages, and the stage count of each path is a priced latency, not an afterthought.
cards.status_basis: measured routed express link; applied to every die

facts.label: SS reach a stage at 833 ps

cards.problem: The HBM die's longest x-broadcast path is 22,869 um of routed wire; the Qwen die needs 8,965 relays relay stations.

naive.title: Use the typical-corner reach
naive.text: A typical-corner figure promises twice the distance per clock; a design priced on it is not signed off at the slow corner.

trick.title: Register every 430.56 um and count the stages
trick.text: The measured slow-corner reach is 504 um a stage at 833 ps; pricing uses a 430.56 um pitch for margin. Each path class is counted from the routed bundle: the x-broadcast is 60 stages at 430.56 um (51 stages at 504 um).

cards.evidence: Routed die global-route record; class bounds per path in the expander.
cards.price: Stages are latency: 22,487 cycles/token a Qwen token for its relays, and the HBM wire terms in the unified ledger.

cards.title: A hold margin that was counted twice
cards.summary: Every die link had its hold allowance charged at both ends: once on the sender's output and once on the receiver's input. Blocks were failing hold by margins that did not exist. Counting it once, at the sender, turned several of them into closed blocks without touching a route.
cards.status_basis: flow rule on main; re-timed routes closed without re-routing
cards.problem: A die link's hold term (50 ps plus uncertainty) was applied as the sender's output minimum delay and again as the receiver's input minimum delay.

naive.title: Each block protects itself
naive.text: Both sides budget for the same physical hold risk, so each sees half a real margin and hold repair chases a violation that is not there (or the route fails).

trick.title: Rule H1: the sender carries it
trick.text: The hold term rides once, on the sender's output min delay; the receiver's input min equals the measured link minimum. Existing routes are re-timed under the corrected constraints without re-routing (resta_hold), and the multi-mode route repairs SS setup and FF hold together.

cards.evidence: Constraints committed (physical/qwen_die_masters/io_ref_skew.sdc); closed under the rule: code SS 234.2 / FF 159.3 ps (results/closure_loop/qfd_embed_ingress_code-0e025d03c/verdict.json); scale SS 236.5 / FF 160.9 ps (results/closure_loop/qfd_embed_ingress_scale-0e025d03c/verdict.json).
cards.price: None in cycles; it removes a fake constraint, it does not relax a real one.

cards.title: Redundancy that survives synthesis
cards.element: kept replicas and prefix adders (ot_v41_kreg, ot_v41_prefix)
cards.summary: To cut fanout, a register is copied so each copy drives a few loads, and adders are written as log-depth prefix trees. Synthesis undoes both unless told not to: it merges identical registers and re-ripples adders. So the copies and the trees are kept explicitly, and counted in the routed netlist.
cards.status_basis: design rule; replica counts checked in routed netlists

facts.label: g_ixb replicas in the routed netlist

cards.problem: Beat assembly in the field spine reads 32 x-buffer banks and selects across 64 lanes from shared indices: one driver, many loads.

naive.title: Copy the register in RTL
naive.text: Yosys sees identical registers and merges them (opt_merge); ABC rebuilds a written prefix adder as a ripple in context. The netlist ends up with the original fanout.

trick.title: Keep-hierarchy replicas and kept prefix trees
trick.text: Every replica is an ot_v41_kreg instance with keep_hierarchy, so it cannot be folded; arithmetic uses explicit log-depth prefix modules marked keep. The routed netlist is checked for the instance counts.

cards.evidence: Routed R=16 spine netlists contain 32 instances g_ixb, 8 instances g_ixq and 64 instances g_sel kept replicas.
cards.price: A few thousand flops a die (about 1.6k replica and pipeline flops in the spine).

naive.note: One driver, 32 loads after opt_merge folds the copies.
